evidence.locator: Install; Supported agents; Highlights; Architecture; Development

evidence.title: waku docs/providers.md
evidence.locator: Transport table; Runtime lifetime; At a glance; Access modes
evidence.finding: Documents provider-native session protocols, background session runtime, steering, cancellation and per-provider permission differences. Model changes may apply live or restart a driver; provider changes restart.

evidence.title: waku Cargo.toml
evidence.locator: Package; GPUI dependencies
evidence.finding: Pinned build manifest declares GPL-3.0-only and native Rust GPUI dependencies.

evidence.title: waku docs/commit-messages.md
evidence.locator: Commit-message generation; Which model; The prompt
evidence.finding: Commit dialog can generate a message using the selected agent CLI. Generation reads Git diff, not conversation history; Claude/Codex use pinned lower-cost models.

evidence.title: waku v0.1.20 release
evidence.locator: v0.1.20 release
evidence.finding: Release published 2 October 2026 with OpenCode session continuity and provider discovery fixes.

evidence.title: Waku homepage FAQ
evidence.locator: FAQ 'Do I need new API keys?', 'Where does my data live?', 'What is the future plan?'
evidence.finding: Says Waku drives the agent CLIs already on your machine with your existing logins, plans and rate limits, and has no Waku account. Cloud agents are planned. No price is shown.

evidence.title: Waku README
evidence.locator: 'Sponsorship'; 'License'
evidence.finding: Says Waku is GPL-3.0 and invites optional support through GitHub Sponsors. It mentions no paid plan.

evidence.title: egoist/waku LICENSE (GPL-3.0)
evidence.locator: License header and preamble
evidence.finding: The code is published under GPL-3.0. That license is about freedom to use, modify and share the code. It does not state a price.

evidence.title: Waku daemon worktree module
evidence.locator: crates/waku-core/src/worktree.rs lines 1-5, release v0.1.20 commit 10bcd72
evidence.finding: The daemon creates an isolated Git worktree for a task beneath ~/.waku/worktrees on first submission when the user chose a new worktree.

evidence.title: Waku desktop composer workspace menu
evidence.locator: src/app/composer.rs lines 2945-2953 and 3397-3410, release v0.1.20 commit 10bcd72
evidence.finding: The native desktop composer offers a 'New worktree' workspace choice, with a base branch, alongside existing worktrees.

evidence.title: Waku general settings anonymous analytics toggle
evidence.locator: src/app/settings.rs lines 430-438 and 591-596, release v0.1.20 commit 10bcd72
evidence.finding: General settings render an anonymous analytics toggle that saves the choice and turns the analytics worker off or on.

evidence.title: Waku analytics module
evidence.locator: src/analytics.rs lines 1-44 and crates/waku-client/src/persistence.rs lines 80-82, release v0.1.20 commit 10bcd72
evidence.finding: Release builds send Umami product analytics without prompts, paths or provider identity; analytics defaults to enabled and any build can opt out with WAKU_DISABLE_ANALYTICS=1.

evidence.title: Waku homepage
evidence.locator: 'Local by architecture' section and footer
evidence.finding: The homepage says projects, sessions and transcripts live on the user's disk with no account, no telemetry and no Waku cloud, and offers a download; it shows no price or paid plan.

evidence.title: Waku README, supported agents
evidence.locator: README.md lines 7-22 (Install) and 41-43, release v0.1.20 commit 10bcd72
evidence.finding: Users install and authenticate at least one supported agent CLI before starting Waku, which detects the CLIs and drives them through each provider's native protocol; Waku installs from a signed download or install script.

evidence.title: Waku apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx
evidence.locator: IndexRoute renders WakuShell; apps/web/README.md dev/build/deploy commands and daemon connection instructions
evidence.finding: The v0.1.20 source release includes a browser workspace route and instructions to launch it with bun --filter @waku/web dev, connect an existing daemon URL/token and configure its allowed browser origin. Build and deployment commands support a user-hosted browser client.

evidence.title: Waku crates/waku-daemon/src/main.rs
evidence.locator: Arguments::parse; crates/waku-daemon/README.md invocation
evidence.finding: Waku ships the product-owned waku-daemon CLI with bind, parent-pid, allow-origin and explicit non-loopback exposure controls. It starts the Waku backend; it is separate from the coding-agent CLIs and is not a headless agent-prompt command.

evidence.title: Waku .github/workflows/release.yml
evidence.locator: Complete release jobs and assets
evidence.finding: The release workflow packages only macOS, Linux and Windows native applications. The repository has a separate browser app, with no native iOS or Android release target.

evidence.title: Waku crates/waku-core/src/server.rs
evidence.locator: ServerOptions allow_shutdown lines 52-62; connection and subscriber lifecycle
evidence.finding: Service-managed daemons keep running when authenticated clients disconnect. The daemon retains provider sessions independently of the attached client; a remote daemon is distinct from a same-host desktop child.

evidence.title: Waku crates/waku-protocol/src/model.rs
evidence.locator: SessionWorkspace enum lines 618-640; crates/waku-core/src/daemon.rs Command::Start; driver/mod.rs start_local; bounded container/VM search
evidence.finding: The complete Waku workspace enum has ordinary Local, NewWorktree and Worktree cases. The daemon starts provider drivers as processes on its own host; no Waku-owned container or VM isolation backend is implemented. Provider-native sandboxing is a separate scope.

evidence.title: Waku crates/waku-protocol/src/protocol.rs
evidence.locator: Command enum and full handler in crates/waku-core/src/daemon.rs; bounded search of core/protocol/src for cron, scheduler, webhook, coordinator, delegate
evidence.finding: The closed command set provides client-driven session starts, prompts, steering, cancellation and session persistence. Source inspection found no Waku coordinator/delegation role, schedule service, external-event run starter or separate issue operations. Provider-native subagents are separate.

evidence.title: Waku crates/waku-protocol/src/model.rs
evidence.locator: Project and AgentSession structs, lines 598 onward and 939-1032; task persistence and protocol operations
evidence.finding: Persisted tasks are AgentSession records with provider, conversation, workspace and run status. Projects group sessions. No separate issue/backlog entity or issue state machine exists in the pinned model or daemon persistence API.

evidence.title: Waku crates/waku-daemon/src/main.rs
evidence.locator: Token authentication and serve options; crates/waku-daemon/README.md security contract
evidence.finding: The daemon authenticates trusted clients with one full-control WAKU_DAEMON_TOKEN and exact allowed browser origins. It has no per-user/workspace roles or enterprise identity/SSO flow.

evidence.title: Waku crates/waku-core/src/daemon.rs
evidence.locator: AttachSession lines 230-243; PromptSubmitted fanout lines 847-871; shared Command::Prompt
evidence.finding: Multiple trusted clients can attach to the same provider runtime, send prompts or steering, and receive the submitted message through the shared event stream. The token gives all clients full control, without individual user attribution.

evidence.title: Waku crates/waku-protocol/src/workspace.rs
evidence.locator: WorkspaceOperation enum, git operations; bounded core and UI search for pull_request, pr create and create_pull
evidence.finding: The product Git API supports branch inspection, checkout, commit and push, but no pull-request creation/management operation. Bounded source inspection found no native PR workflow. Agents can still invoke external tools on their own.
